what_its_for: Clarithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. This includes infections of the lungs (such as pneumonia and bronchitis), sinuses, throat, skin, and ears. It is also used to treat stomach ulcers caused by a bacteria called H. pylori, and to prevent or treat infections in people with HIV. It only works against bacterial infections and will NOT work for colds, flu, or other viral infections.
how_to_take: Take clarithromycin exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take the regular tablets or liquid with or without food. If you are taking the extended-release tablets (Biaxin XL), take them WITH food and swallow them whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. If you are taking the liquid suspension, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully using a medical spoon or oral syringe, not a regular kitchen spoon. Finish all of your medication even if you start feeling better. Stopping early can allow the infection to come back or make the antibiotic stop working.
dosing: The dose depends on your specific infection, your age, weight, and kidney function. Common adult doses range from 250 mg to 500 mg taken every 12 hours (twice a day) for 7 to 14 days. Extended-release tablets are usually taken once daily. Children's doses are based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions for your exact dose and how long to take it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. For the liquid suspension, store at room temperature and throw away any unused liquid after 14 days — do not refrigerate the liquid. Keep all medications out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking clarithromycin with certain other medications, as serious interactions can occur. Do not take it with colchicine if you have kidney or liver problems. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while on this medication, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood. Do not take antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium at the same time as this medicine — if you need an antacid, take it at least 2 hours before or after your dose. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting clarithromycin, because it interacts with many drugs including blood thinners, cholesterol medicines (statins), and heart medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical attention right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing); severe stomach pain, cramping, or watery or bloody diarrhea (even if it occurs weeks after finishing your antibiotic, as this could be a serious bowel infection called C. diff); chest pain or irregular heartbeat; yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness (signs of liver problems); muscle weakness or pain; or any signs of a new or worsening infection. Also contact your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting clarithromycin. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of antibiotics as prescribed, even if you feel completely better before it is done. Stopping too soon can let the bacteria grow back and become harder to treat.
special_populations: Tell your doctor before taking clarithromycin if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as your doctor will need to weigh the risks and benefits. If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to lower your dose or monitor you more closely. Clarithromycin can be used in children but the dose is based on the child's weight. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially heartbeat changes. Always inform your doctor of all your medical conditions before starting this medication.
